corrections.before: Robert C. Martin argued that 'a mess made through ignorance is not debt at all'; Fowler's reply that 'the quadrant keeps the useful question ... while still marking reckless debt'
corrections.after: In a 2009 post Martin argued 'a mess is not a technical debt': debt means reasoned trade-offs under real constraints and code must still be kept clean; Fowler replied that whether a flaw 'is' debt is the wrong question and a mess is reckless debt
corrections.reason: 'Through ignorance' is Fowler's paraphrase; Martin's own post calls a mess 'never rational' and 'based on laziness and unprofessionalism'. Fowler's reply restated from his quadrant page.
YouTube metadata for pqeJFYwnkjE (Ward Cunningham, 'Debt Metaphor'): published 2009-02-14; the C2 transcript page carries Ward's CC-BY licence note.
